ideas.label: Caro-Slav Structure
ideas.summary: The Caro-Slav family is defined by one side's advanced d-pawn against a restrained opposing center. Plans revolve around challenging that pawn and freeing the cramped pieces behind it.

source_books: Maneuvering: The Art of Piece Play

ideas.label: Caro-Slav Structure
ideas.summary: In Caro-Slav structures, compare breaks against the front of the chain with breaks against its base. Piece placement decides whether the position opens favorably or leaves a permanent weak pawn.

ideas.label: Caro-Slav Structure
ideas.principle: Release pieces trapped by your own pawn
ideas.summary: If an advanced e-pawn merely blocks your bishop and rook, returning or sacrificing it can restore coordination. Do not attack a distant pawn while the opponent has a protected passer or a forcing kingside advance.
